SpaceX just acquired Cursor, triggering immediate shifts in the developer AI landscape.

Here is what is happening in AI engineering today.

🚀 OpenAI is winding down its contract to provide OpenAI models to the Cursor editor following Cursor's acquisition by SpaceX.

📉 Anthropic is ending its extended use limits for Claude on August 31st, meaning users will get less usage for the same price.

🐞 Developers are reporting significant frustration with Opus 5, noting missing tasks and buggy code that require redoing work up to 10 times when fable credits run out.

🎵 StemDeck has launched on GitHub as a free, open-source, and local AI stem separator.

💻 A new community experiment shows how to turn LLM memory systems into a functional tool for program analysis.

As software engineers, our day-to-day productivity is increasingly tied to the stability of external AI platforms. When acquisitions occur or API limits are suddenly adjusted, it directly impacts our development speed and operational costs.

Building redundancy into our local environments—using open-source tools and maintaining the ability to swap backend models programmatically—is becoming a necessity rather than an afterthought.

We must focus on building resilient systems that do not break when a single provider changes their terms of service.

How are you adapting your development workflow to handle changing API limits and shifting model access?
